A1.justification: Both PDFs describe TopoDiffusionNet by the same authors, and their text, equations, tables and figures are readable. V1 includes Appendices A–F; the supplied v2 ends with references and omits those appendices, allowing their absence to be established.

before.justification: V1 reports original generation experiments on four main datasets, loss ablations, timestep analyses and additional appendix experiments.

after.justification: V2 retains original four-dataset results in Table 1, the additional comparison in Table 2, loss ablations and timestep analysis.

M1.justification: The topology-conditioned ADM architecture, learned constraint embedding, persistent-homology partition and preservation/denoising losses remain unchanged. Removing the appendix comparison with sinusoidal embeddings does not change the proposed method.

E1.justification: Shapes, COCO, CREMI and Google Maps coverage remains unchanged. V2 omits the synthetic circular-ring dataset and standalone-hole scenario from v1 Appendix E, removing evaluation of holes independent of the image boundary.

E2.justification: The main comparator sets, including Paiss et al. in Table 2, are unchanged. V2 drops the additional Stable Diffusion, DALL·E 3 and Attention Refocusing comparisons for the CREMI/Google Maps cases in v1 Appendix D and Figure 10; these methods remain comparators elsewhere.

E3.justification: V1 Appendix F tests learned linear-layer versus sinusoidal constraint encodings with the topological loss retained; v2 removes this controlled configuration comparison. Shared experiments retain the stated resolution, diffusion steps and evaluation sample counts. Missing training disclosures do not establish changed training settings.

E4.justification: V2 removes the COCO low-versus-high-count analysis, additional one-dimensional baseline failure examples, standalone-hole generalization test and encoding-network ablation from Appendices C–F. This substantially narrows supplementary validation, although the loss-component, loss-weight and timestep analyses remain.

E5.justification: Both report means and standard deviations across constraint values and use the same unpaired t-test and significance markings. Removed appendix results used the existing uncertainty-reporting practice; no seed or repeated-run reporting change is documented.

E6.justification: Tables 1–4 retain all numerical values, and Figure 8 retains its findings. However, v2 removes several distinct result sets: standalone-hole results in Table 6, encoding comparisons in Table 7, count-stratified accuracy in Figure 9 and supplementary qualitative examples. For example, v1's standalone-hole accuracies of 0.95 ± 0.03 for TDN and 0.79 ± 0.12 for ADM-T disappear.

T1.justification: Section 3 retains the mathematical definitions, Equations 1–5, loss construction and differentiability argument. Removing the one-dimensional explanatory panels does not revise the underlying mathematics.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the claims of first integrating topology with diffusion models, controlling zero- and one-dimensional structures through a topological loss, and demonstrating improvements on four datasets.

C2.justification: V2 loses Appendix D's qualification that pretrained baselines' poor electron-microscopy outputs are understandable given their training coverage. It also removes Appendix E's explicit discussion of applicability beyond boundary-defined holes. The main interpretations of the loss components and denoising behavior remain unchanged.

D1.justification: V2 replaces a future code-release promise with a project repository link and explicitly names ControlNet's SD1.5 backbone. However, removing Appendices A–B deletes training-set composition, white-border preprocessing, RTX A6000 hardware, batch size 16, learning rate 2 × 10−5 and CREMI-specific ControlNet fine-tuning disclosures. Cubical Ripser is retained through relocation to Section 4.

R1.justification: V2 adds Xu et al. (2024) on topological segmentation and removes the Vaswani et al. (2017) and Tengfei Wang et al. (2022) references associated with omitted appendix discussions. The broader research positioning and novelty claims remain unchanged.

P1.justification: The main section order and most prose remain unchanged. V2 converts related-work subsections into paragraph headings, updates author/publication text, adds reproducibility and acknowledgment paragraphs, and removes the appendix roadmap and cross-references along with the appendices.

P2.justification: V2 adopts the ICLR layout and substantially resizes and regroups retained displays. Figures 4 and 5 lose their one-dimensional panels and corresponding caption explanations; Figures 9–11 and Tables 5–7 disappear. Figures 6–7 and Tables 1–4 are consolidated into denser arrangements.

improvement.justification: The core method and main quantitative evidence remain intact, and the code link improves access information. Nevertheless, deleting the appendices removes useful generalization and ablation evidence plus important dataset, preprocessing and training disclosures. The supplied v2 is consequently less complete and transparent, producing a limited net decline despite the access improvement.
